Case Study Page: Content for Bobby

Alex (Deal Architect) | 2026-03-12 Maps 1:1 to Steffen's 16-section design spec at projects/steffen/case-study-design-spec.md Bobby: drop this content into the template. Every section below matches a section in the spec.

Section 0: Hero

Micro-label: CASE STUDY

Headline: WE BUILT THE SYSTEM WE SELL.

Subhead: 12 AI agents. 280+ commits. 2 weeks. $0 new hires. Here's what happened when a creative agency stopped talking about AI and started running on it.

Scroll indicator text: READ THE STORY

Section 1: The Problem (Before)

Micro-label: BEFORE

Headline: ONE PERSON. EVERY ROLE.

Body copy (paragraph 1): AOM is a creative production company in Phoenix. Video, web, brand, social. Two people, a dozen clients, and a pipeline held together by memory and momentum. Patrik Matheson ran operations, strategy, client relationships, outreach, quality control, and creative production. All of it. Every day.

Body copy (paragraph 2): The bottleneck was never talent. It was time. One person physically cannot produce the work, find the next client, follow up on invoices, check every deliverable at every screen size, and keep the brand consistent across every touchpoint. Something always slipped. And when you're the only one who knows everything, you can't take a day off without the whole system pausing.

Pain Points Grid (6 cards)

Card 01: "OUTREACH WAS MANUAL" Every prospecting email was written from scratch. No templates, no tracking, no follow-up system. Leads went cold because nobody was watching the inbox at scale.

Card 02: "CLIENT TRACKING LIVED IN PATRIK'S HEAD" Which client was waiting on a deliverable? Who needed a follow-up? What was overdue? The answers existed in one place: Patrik's memory. If he forgot, it fell through.

Card 03: "QUALITY CONTROL WAS REACTIVE" Bugs got caught when a client mentioned them. Pages went live without being checked at every breakpoint. Accessibility issues only surfaced after launch, never before.

Card 04: "BRAND CONSISTENCY WAS LUCK" Fonts drifted. Colors shifted. Spacing varied between pages. Without a system enforcing standards, every deliverable was a coin flip on whether it matched the brand.

Card 05: "OPERATIONS RAN ON MEMORY" What needs to happen next? Who's working on what? What's blocked? There was no dashboard, no task router, no system that surfaced priorities. Just a mental checklist that reset every morning.

Card 06: "24/7 AVAILABILITY WAS IMPOSSIBLE" Client messages at 11 PM sat until morning. Weekend requests waited until Monday. Urgent fixes waited for Patrik to wake up, check his phone, and context-switch from whatever he was doing.

Section 2: The Decision (The Turn)

Micro-label: THE TURN

Headline: WHAT IF THE AGENCY RAN ITSELF?

Body copy (paragraph 1): The conventional answer is hiring. An outreach coordinator. A project manager. A QA tester. A brand manager. That's $200,000 to $280,000 a year in salary alone, before benefits, before office space, before the months of training, before you realize two of the four aren't the right fit and start the process again.

Body copy (paragraph 2): Patrik chose a different path. Using Claude Code as the foundation, he built specialized AI agents, each one owning a defined part of the business. Not a chatbot that answers questions. Not a plugin that automates one workflow. A full operations layer. Twelve agents working in a coordinated pipeline, handing work to each other, enforcing standards, and running 24 hours a day without supervision.

Pull Quote

Quote text: "Isn't it smart for me as a small business owner to help build tailored solutions for people since I've been able to do it for myself?"

Attribution: Patrik Matheson, AOM

Section 3: The System (After)

Micro-label: AFTER

Headline: 12 AGENTS. ONE SYSTEM. ZERO NEW HIRES.

3a. Pipeline Visualization

Pipeline nodes (left to right):

Node Agent Name Role Label
E Elon System
M Mom Operations
A Alex Strategy
S Steffen Brand
B Bobby Build
Q Elmo QA
P Patrik Approve

Note below pipeline: Every deliverable flows through this chain automatically. Patrik only touches the final approval.

3b. Agent Cards Grid (12 cards)

Card: JACOB

  • Title: OUTREACH ENGINE
  • Description: Researches prospects, writes personalized emails, tracks responses across every campaign.
  • Replaced: Manual copy-paste emails with no tracking

Card: MOM

  • Title: CHIEF OF STAFF
  • Description: Scans priorities, routes work to the right agent, closes loops across every open thread.
  • Replaced: Patrik mentally juggling every open task

Card: PAIGE

  • Title: CLIENT HEALTH
  • Description: Monitors client satisfaction, flags risks before they escalate, tracks every deliverable status.
  • Replaced: Client relationships tracked in Patrik's head

Card: ELMO

  • Title: QUALITY GATE
  • Description: Screenshots every page at 5 breakpoints, checks accessibility, catches regressions before anything goes live.
  • Replaced: Bugs only caught on manual review

Card: BOBBY

  • Title: WEB BUILDER
  • Description: Builds pages from design specs and deploys to production. Hours, not weeks.
  • Replaced: Weeks of development time per page

Card: STEFFEN

  • Title: BRAND DIRECTOR
  • Description: Enforces visual identity across every deliverable. Every font, color, and spacing decision runs through brand standards.
  • Replaced: Inconsistent visuals across deliverables

Card: CLEO

  • Title: CONTENT PRODUCER
  • Description: Video editing workflows, audio generation, and content production pipelines from raw footage to final cut.
  • Replaced: Manual video editing and content creation

Card: TONY

  • Title: SOCIAL MEDIA
  • Description: Multi-platform posting, scheduling, and content distribution across LinkedIn, Instagram, and TikTok.
  • Replaced: Manual posting with no scheduling

Card: ELON

  • Title: SYSTEM ADMIN
  • Description: Infrastructure monitoring, credential rotation, health checks, and security across the entire stack.
  • Replaced: No monitoring, no credential management

Card: ALEX

  • Title: DEAL ARCHITECT
  • Description: Offer strategy, pricing models, competitive analysis, and proposal frameworks that feed the sales pipeline.
  • Replaced: Ad-hoc strategy, never documented

Card: STEVE

  • Title: AI ADVISORY LEAD
  • Description: Product packaging, ROI modeling, and audit frameworks for the AI advisory service line.
  • Replaced: No product structure or pricing

Card: RELAY

  • Title: 24/7 BRIDGE
  • Description: Telegram relay with sub-2-second response time and a watchdog that ensures nothing sits unread.
  • Replaced: Messages sitting unread until morning

Section 4: The Numbers (Light Section)

Micro-label: RESULTS

Headline: THE NUMBERS DON'T LIE.

4a. Metrics Callout Grid (6 cards)

Number Suffix Label Context
12 + Specialized AI Agents Running 24/7
280 + Commits Shipped In the first two weeks
~2 hrs Time to Build a Page From spec to live on site
51 + Outreach Emails Sent Personalized and tracked
$0 Additional Headcount Zero new hires
24/7 Operational Uptime Relay + watchdog + agents

4b. Cost Comparison Table

Left column header: TRADITIONAL APPROACH Right column header: AOM'S AI SYSTEM

Role Traditional Salary AOM Agent AOM Cost
Outreach coordinator $45-65k/year Jacob agent $0
QA tester $50-70k/year Elmo agent $0
Project manager $55-75k/year Mom agent $0
Brand manager $50-70k/year Steffen agent $0
After-hours coverage Overtime or missed messages 24/7 relay + watchdog $0
Total $200-280k/year AI Operations System Fraction of one hire

Footer note: AOM's system isn't replacing creative work. It's replacing the operational overhead that keeps creative people from doing creative work.

Section 5: Day in the Life

Micro-label: A DAY IN THE LIFE

Headline: WHAT 24 HOURS LOOKS LIKE.

Timeline Entries

7:00 AM | RELAY | Stone MESSAGE RECEIVED Patrik sends a Telegram message: "Check Ambition site, footer looks off on mobile."

7:01 AM | RELAY | Stone RELAY INJECTION Message picked up via hook. No polling, no delay. Injected into the active session in under 2 seconds.

7:02 AM | BOBBY | Orange BOBBY LAUNCHES Reads the request, pulls the repo, identifies the CSS issue in the footer component.

7:08 AM | BOBBY | Orange FIX COMMITTED Code pushed to production. Mom auto-launches to scan the pipeline for downstream effects.

7:09 AM | ELMO | Sage QA RUNS Elmo screenshots the page at 5 breakpoints. Desktop, laptop, tablet portrait, tablet landscape, mobile. Checks for regressions against the last passing state.

7:12 AM | MOM | Sage CONFIRMED LIVE Patrik gets confirmation: "Footer fixed. Elmo QA passed at all 5 breakpoints. Live on site."

While Patrik's on a shoot... | SYSTEM | Stone BACKGROUND AGENTS Jacob sends 15 outreach emails to construction companies. Paige scans client health across all active accounts. Steffen catches a font-weight deviation on the briefs page and routes it to Bobby.

11:00 PM | RELAY | Stone AFTER HOURS Patrik's asleep. A message comes in from a client. The watchdog catches it, sends Patrik a "handling it" notice, and defers the message for morning pickup. Nothing sits unread.

"12 Minutes" Callout

Big text: 12 MINUTES

Subtext: From request to live fix, with QA. While Patrik was still pouring coffee.

Section 6: The Bridge + CTA

Micro-label: YOUR BUSINESS

Headline: WE BUILT IT FOR US. NOW WE BUILD IT FOR YOU.

Body copy (paragraph 1): Everything on this page is real. The system is running right now, as you read this. The agents that built this website are the same agents that sent the email or LinkedIn post that brought you here. This is not a concept. It is not a roadmap. It is a production system handling real operations for a real business.

Body copy (paragraph 2): The question is not whether AI can run a small business's back office. We proved it can. The question is what it would look like for yours. Your workflows are different. Your bottlenecks are different. Your team is different. But the pattern is the same: find what eats your time, automate it, and give you back the hours to do the work that actually grows your business.

  • Description: 6 inputs. 30 seconds. See what AI operations could save your business.

  • Description: The $2,500 AI Operations Audit maps your exact workflows, not industry averages. You walk away with a blueprint whether you hire us or not.
  • Button: BOOK YOUR AUDIT
  • Link: /book

Card 3: TALK TO US

  • Icon: MessageCircle
  • Description: 15 minutes. No cost. No pitch. Just a straight conversation about what's possible for your business.
  • Button: SCHEDULE A CALL
  • Link: /book

Headline: STOP DOING EVERYTHING YOURSELF.

Subhead: Your business deserves the same system we built for ours.
